habitat_summary: Neritic to oceanic; epipelagic to mesopelagic. Two tagged animals moved from near-surface to deep daytime waters.

season_note: IMARPE reports main spawning from October to January and secondary activity in August.

peru_coast_range_note: Peru, 10 to more than 500 nautical miles offshore.
fishery_note: IMARPE reports artisanal and industrial fleets.
notes: Two tagged squid reached 1200 m (2017, p. 174); this is not a population limit. Review status: No thermal optimum reported in reviewed sources. Existing season and El Nino references are present; remote recheck: no accesible (timeout or 502).

habitat_summary: Benthic in semi-protected bays on sedimentary bottoms; also sandy or muddy bottoms with shells and macroalgae.
temperature_note: Lab juveniles were tested at 17 and 22 C in Peru; treatment temperatures, not limits or optimum.
season_note: Spawning occurs year-round, stronger September to May.
el_nino_response_note: An IMARPE 2024 assessment reports poor population condition after the 2023-24 warm event despite expected density increase.
notes: Section 2.7.2 reports typical 5-40 m; IMARPE species record gives a broader intertidal-to-95 m distribution. Review status: No thermal optimum reported in reviewed sources. Machine-readable species landings pending: public monthly charts verified in F26; data endpoint not verified.

season_note: Spawning occurs year-round, with spring and summer peaks.
el_nino_response_note: IMARPE diet observations during 1982-83 and 1997-98 El Nino differed by site; no coast-wide response inferred.

habitat_summary: Benthodemersal; IMARPE assessment reports concentrations at 100-200 m.
temperature_note: Peru field bottom temperatures: 10-16 C on normal cruise and 14.5-22.3 C during El Nino; not limits or optimum.
season_note: Main spawning in winter-spring; secondary spawning in summer-autumn.
el_nino_response_note: IMARPE reports inverted distribution and 14.5-22.3 C bottom temperatures in the 1983 El Nino cruise.
notes: WoRMS accepts Merluccius peruanus; Merluccius gayi peruanus is retained as historical synonym. Review status: A closed published upper depth of 800 m is documented in F41; the original guide wording remains in depth_note.
depth_note: The guide records depths from 50 m to more than 600 m; no closed maximum is given. F41 states the species can be caught from near the surface to 800 m depth (fishing depth range).
